content: The diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) have been a subject of global discussion, with the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria being widely adopted. These criteria are often referred to as the one-step strategy for GDM screening. This approach has achieved significant international recognition as the preferred method for diagnosing GDM. However, comparative studies evaluating the one-step method against the traditional two-step method in terms of population-wide outcomes have yielded inconsistent findings. These discrepancies highlight the need for further research and refinement to optimize screening and diagnostic strategies for GDM.
